Conflict Minerals Policy



 The Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) adopted annual disclosure
 requirements in connection with the conflict minerals provision of the Dodd-Frank Wall
 Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act, requiring publicly traded companies to
 disclose whether certain minerals necessary to the functionality or production of
 products manufactured or contracted to be manufactured originated in the Democratic
 Republic of Congo and its nine neighboring countries (the “DRC”). These certain
 minerals referred to as “conflict minerals” include tantalum (columbite-tantalite), tin
 (cassiterite), tungsten (wolframite) and gold (“3TGs”).

 Pace is committed to complying with all the conflict mineral requirements under the Act
 as issued by the SEC.

 Pace Industries (“Pace”) supports the humanitarian goal of ending the violence and
 human rights violations in the DRC, which are believed to have been partially financed
 by the exploitation and trade of conflict minerals. Pace strives to have a conflict free
 supply chain and is committed to working with its suppliers to increase transparency
 regarding the origin of minerals contained in its products. Pace requires its suppliers to
 undertake reasonable due diligence with their suppliers to identify whether any of the
 products supplied to Pace contain 3TGs sourced from the DRC and, if so, whether the
 mines and smelters identified are certified as “conflict free” by an independent third
 party.










 Hal Grant, REP, CHMM
 Corporate Director
 Technical & Regulatory Affairs
